ledger.claim: The rider's first burden element under POL-RD-08 is satisfied on the face of the bundle: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-09112, and their timestamps agree - the trace runs 14:10:00 to 14:32:00 SGT against trip_record.started_at 14:10:00 and ended_at 14:32:00. No identifier or timestamp mismatch of the kind POL-RD-10(2) or POL-RD-10(4) turns on is present, so the claim is not defeated at the threshold.

Measured as POL-RD-01 requires - trace distance against the booked optimal, because gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs where the two distance fields disagree - the driver's own trace records 11.5 km against a booked optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 1.5 km. That is more than three times the 0.8 km absolute limb of POL-RD-01, and the trace carrying it is clean: 133 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, and no gap above 30 seconds.

Nothing on this record excuses the excess. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-09112-01, is MISSING - status MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - so POL-RD-03 cannot be run for want of the advisory record it requires, and the driver names no closure, queue or incident in the chat log, whose sole message is the rider's own observation at 14:21:40. The counterparty's bare denial that he stayed on ordinary through roads and made no additional stop cites no evidence ID and, under POL-RD-08, carries no weight and does not discharge the driver's burden of pointing to a specific artifact and a specific clause.

The rider's own profile does not narrow the claim: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated are both 0, so the additional corroboration requirement in the last sentence of POL-RD-08 is not engaged, and the claim stands to be assessed on this trip's evidence alone.

I state plainly what the record shows on the one element the rider cannot carry: the trace's own derived excess_pct is 15.00 against POL-RD-01's 20% limb. The two limbs of POL-RD-01 are conjunctive - the excess must exceed both 20% of the optimal distance and 0.8 km - so although the 1.5 km excess clears the absolute limb, it does not clear the percentage limb, and on these figures the deviation is not established and the rider's monetary claim cannot be sustained. For completeness, had both limbs been met, the POL-RD-02 arithmetic on the fare_breakdown gives charged_total 19.39 less recomputed_fare 17.70, a refund of 1.69 rounded up to 1.70, and that would be a PARTIAL_REFUND, the refund being 8.7% of the charge and nowhere near the 90% full-refund share. I do not press a figure the clause does not authorise.

The governing measurement is the trace, and the trace is what the policy makes decisive. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 11.5 km against a booked optimal of 10.0 km on the trip record, an excess of 1.5 km. That is 15.00% of the optimal distance, and POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km before a deviation exists. The percentage test fails, so no deviation is established on this trip and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the journey.

Both establishment tests in POL-RD-01 must pass, and the absolute limb cannot carry the claim alone. I do not dispute that the 1.5 km excess clears the 0.8 km absolute threshold, but the 20% relative threshold is not met at 15.00%, and the clause is explicit that both tests must pass. One satisfied limb is not a deviation.

The excess is measured after any adjustment under POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05 or POL-RD-12, and no adjustment is available on this record: the trip record shows amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null with no pickup or dropoff amendment timestamps, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and is not run; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not a pooled product, so the matched-itinerary baseline of POL-RD-12 does not apply. The 15.00% figure stands as the final excess with nothing reducing it.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02 never runs. The recomputation it describes is conditional on a POL-RD-01 finding, and the fare breakdown's own arithmetic — a recomputed fare of 17.70 against 19.39 charged, a difference of 1.69 — is therefore not an amount the rider is entitled to, however exactly that figure matches the sum claimed. Without the threshold finding there is no arithmetic entitlement to move.

POL-RD-01 preserves one refund route even where no deviation exists — a billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) — and there is nothing on this fare to correct. The ERP total is $0.00 with an empty gantry list, and the airport surcharge is $0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport (it runs Mandai Estate to Seletar West). No charge line is unmatched to the trace, so no standalone refund is due and POL-RD-10(8) has no line to fire on.

On a rider-filed dispute, NO_ACTION means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present state stands: fare_breakdown.payment_status stays CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd stays $0.00. That is precisely the position this trip's metered fare supports, so NO_ACTION is the driver-favourable outcome here, not a neutral one.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08. Limb (a) is satisfied — trip identifier TRP-09112 and the 14:10:00 pickup timestamp match across the trip record, the trace and the fare breakdown — but limb (b) is not, because the excess measured from an unimpaired trace is 15.00% and the POL-RD-01 threshold is 20%. The burden therefore never shifts to the driver and the driver is not called on to invoke any exculpatory clause.

No escalation trigger fires on this record. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: it carries 133 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps list and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds, so none of limbs (a) to (c) is met and POL-RD-10(3) cannot apply. The case is also not finely balanced — the rider's own clean trace measures the excess below the establishment threshold — so POL-RD-10(7) is not engaged either, and ESCALATE, which would hold the disputed amount rather than resolve it, is not warranted.

I cite the absent traffic advisory and disclose its impairment: EV-ADVIS-09112-01 carries status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, so it can carry no fact and its absence is itself citable — no advisory covers this road. But the driver asserts no external traffic cause, and names no advisory identifier, so under POL-RD-13 this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact: POL-RD-03 cannot be run, the driver does not ask the tribunal to run it, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged by it.

No repeat-deviation uplift is available against this driver. The driver profile records deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 610, so the POL-RD-06 pattern test — three or more flags in 90 days, or a flag-to-trip ratio of 0.05 or more — is not met, and a trip that is not a material deviation and is not a deviation at all cannot support the (b) uplift. I cite those two fields only because POL-RD-06 names them; the remaining profile fields are context only and ground nothing.

The chat log adds nothing to the rider's side. It holds a single rider message sent at 14:21:40 — 'This looks a little longer than the route shown at booking' — which names no road, identifies no place and carries a null waypoint_hint, and the driver made no additional stop. It is an observation mid-trip, not an instruction, and it is not evidence of a measured excess that the trace does not show.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides have run the same arithmetic, and it decides the case. Under POL-RD-01 the governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km — 11.5 km, not the rounded trip_record copy — against the booked optimal of 10.0 km, an excess of 1.5 km, or 15.00% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to exceed BOTH 20% of optimal_distance_km AND 0.8 km in absolute terms, and the two limbs are conjunctive. The 0.8 km limb passes; the 20% limb (2.0 km) does not, so no deviation is established and POL-RD-01 directs NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The rider's claimed figure of 1.69 is the POL-RD-02 recomputation, and it does not arise: POL-RD-02 runs only after a POL-RD-01 finding. For transparency, the arithmetic it describes would have been charged_total 19.39 less recomputed_fare 17.70 = 1.69, rounded up to 1.70, but it is not an entitlement here and the rider's advocate rightly does not press it. No billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) is available either: the ERP total is 0.00 with an empty gantry list and the airport surcharge is 0.00, so no charge line is unmatched to the trace and the 'save for' route in POL-RD-01 opens nothing. The exculpatory clauses the driver might reach for — POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-12 — do not run, and nothing turns on that: because the excess fails the POL-RD-01 threshold the rider never shifts the burden under POL-RD-08, so the driver's denial (which cites no evidence ID) needs no corroboration and its silence costs nothing. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-09112-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so it can carry no fact; because no party asserts an external traffic cause or cites that identifier, POL-RD-13 governs — the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, POL-RD-03 cannot be run, and POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)–(c) (133 fixes at a 10-second interval, no gap above 30 seconds, 100% coverage), so POL-RD-10(3) is not engaged either, and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires. No referral issues: the POL-RD-06 repeat-deviation test is not met (deviation_flags_90d 0 against completed_trips_90d 610) and there is no billing-integrity finding to record. Outcome: NO_ACTION. On this rider-filed dispute the present state stands — payment_status remains CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00, and no charge or refund moves. Confidence 0.95, above the 0.70 floor, resting on the gps_trace and trip_record, each at full weight 1.0.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
